body:
PR #1993 for BUG-1295 — your drift guard is implemented properly, and the sweep closed the class smaller than either of us expected

Open on bug-1295, +308. I wrote the prompt so no verdict from me, but I verified the one thing the whole spec rests on rather than taking it from the report.

YOUR GUARD IS REAL. The test file asserts the fixture messages share ZERO substrings with every old trigger — and it carries a meta-assertion that the fixture itself does not accidentally contain one, which would otherwise make the test pass while proving nothing. Messages like "the automatic reconciliation could not complete unattended" and "declining to publish — origin moved in a way we cannot safely overwrite" still classify as StaleBaseConflict, on exit code alone. That is your "a test must FAIL when wording drifts without classification following", built the right way round.

The mechanism: exit codes 17 and 18 as shared constants in pr_rebase, plus a sentinel error type that bail sites wrap their message in and `main_entry` downcasts to select the process exit code. The printed prose is untouched, so humans keep the message and the machine stops reading it. That is the producer owning the classification, which is what you asked for.

THE SWEEP CAME BACK SMALLER THAN THE SPEC ASSUMED, and the reasoning is worth your eye because it is the part I cannot verify cheaply. Of the six sites, three needed fixing and three did not:

  - the interactive-mode "rebase hit N conflict(s)" eprintln is unreachable through the orchestrator's --no-smoke call path
  - rebase_cmd.rs belongs to the separate `aida rebase` command, whose consumer only checks .status() and never reads text
  - the "Force-pushing would DROP" prose is diagnostic output printed immediately before a bail that is now typed, so it is covered rather than separate

It then swept every other place lib.rs, pr_cmd.rs and queue_cmd.rs spawn an `aida` subprocess with captured output, and found no other text-matching. The remaining `.contains(...)` classifiers in the codebase read EXTERNAL tool output — CI rollup status, `gh pr merge` text, SQLite lock messages, OS OOM and disk strings — which it argued is a different coupling class and out of scope.

I think that distinction is right, and it is also the load-bearing judgement in the PR: if it is wrong, the class is not closed and we will find the next instance the same way we found this one. Worth a reader who did not make the argument. The external-tool cases are genuinely different — we do not control gh's wording and cannot give it an exit code — but "we do not control it" is a reason to be MORE careful about matching its prose, not less, so there may be a sibling spec in there rather than a non-issue.

Reported, not re-run by me: 5097 tests pass, fmt clean, and the two existing story_429 fixtures were updated from exit 1 to exit 17/18 rather than left to pass by accident.

The pre-commit provenance gate caught two `///` trace-marker leaks in pr_rebase.rs on the first commit attempt. Five of eight lanes now. It is the most productive gate we have.

BUG-1294 is still running. That is the other lane.
